_LOCAL NEWS_🇱🇰

Sri Lanka services expands at higher rate in October 2026: PMI
Sri Lanka’s services sector expanded at a higher rate in October 2026, according to a Purchasing Managers Index compiled by the central bank, which registered an index value of 62.5, compared to 60.5 the previous month.“Business Activity expanded, driven primarily by improvements in other personal services, with notable contributions from financial services and goods transportation,” CBSL said.
Reference: https://tinyurl.com/ypfany2p

Sri Lanka manufacturing PMI expands in October, driven by anticipated seasonal demand
Sri Lanka’s manufacturing sector expanded in October 2026, registering a value of 55.3 on a Purchasing Managers Index compiled by the central bank, from 53.0 the previous month. “This expansion was broad-based, with all sub-indices remaining above the neutral threshold,” CBSL said, noting the outlook remains favourable, underpinned by anticipated demand during the upcoming festive season.
Reference:https://tinyurl.com/4nmz78um

People’s Bank sustains strong earnings momentum with LKR 52.1 billion pre-tax profit for the nine months ended September 30, 2026
People’s Bank delivered a strong financial performance for the nine months ended September 30,2026, building on its earnings momentum and demonstrating financial resilience in an evolving global and domestic economic environment.Strong growth across core income streams reinforced the Bank’s earnings momentum during the nine months ended September 30,2026. Total operating income rose by 18.7% to LKR 145.1 billion, from LKR 122.2 billion in the corresponding period of the previous year, while net interest income increased by 21.5% to LKR 126.2 billion from LKR 103.9 billion.
Reference: https://tinyurl.com/mr2dw53r

Tea output rebounds in October
Sri Lanka’s tea production edged up 0.37% year-on-year to 22.07 MnKg in October. A sharp recovery in High Grown and Medium Grown output offset a decline in Low Grown teas, John Keells PLC said yesterday, citing Sri Lanka Tea Board data. Output was 0.08 MnKg above October 2025 and 0.79 MnKg, or 3.71%, above October 2024. “Sri Lanka’s tea production in October was close to last year’s level, up 0.37%,” John Keells said.
Reference: https://tinyurl.com/555xuf56

Plenty Foods acquires 71% of Convenience Foods for Rs. 3.98 b
Plenty Foods Ltd., yesterday acquired a controlling 71.38% stake in Convenience Foods (Lanka) PLC (CFL) for Rs. 3.98 billion.Plenty Foods bought 1,962,977 ordinary shares in CFL at Rs. 2,025.75 per share. The shares changed hands in a crossing on the Colombo Stock Exchange.Prior to the acquisition, the purchaser did not hold any shares in CFL. The  company reported assets of Rs. 1,578.86 a share as of end-September 2026. CBL Investments Ltd was the top shareholder with a 71.38% followed by Dawi Investment Trust at 10.35% and JB Cocoshell Ltd., 6.03%.

China says Xi-Putin-Trump meeting has 'groundbreaking significance'
China's Foreign Ministry said on Monday that this week's trilateral meeting between the Chinese, US and Russian leaders is of "groundbreaking significance" and will promote world peace ‌and stability.
The meeting between Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin will take place on Thursday in China's southern city of Shenzhen, the site of this week's APEC summit.

Wall Street ends sharply lower on AI jitters ahead of Nvidia results, Anthropic IPO
A broad selloff dragged US stocks lower on Monday as fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO soured enthusiasm for AI stocks, raising the stakes for the chipmaker's earnings report ‌on Tuesday and Anthropic's initial public offering later in the week.
The risk-off sentiment gathered momentum as the session progressed, with the S&P 500 dropping nearly 2% and the Dow falling more than 1.4%. The Nasdaq suffered the steepest percentage loss, tumbling 2.

5%, as the Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index weighed on the tech-heavy index. The SOX lost 5.3%.

Vehicle Market 2026: Electric shift continues, but will demand recover?
Sri Lanka’s vehicle market peaked in May as buyers rushed ahead of tighter LTV limits and the import surcharge, and demand has eased since. The shift to electric has reshaped the market, with EVs leading cars and hybrids gaining ground in SUVs, while commercial vehicles held steady on business demand and fewer financing restrictions. With the surcharge extended to December and financing still tight, we expect a subdued end to the year.
